answer: The quartz multiplier is published, charged in whisper, and ridge lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4754 identities would post 1391 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
